races.name: Sky Sports Racing Juvenile Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hello Garda
runners_data.note: Smart form figures on Good ground (1W3P in similar conditions) and a 43-day break for John Joseph Hanlon looks positive, but this is a genuine hold-up horse pushed forward on the map — it will need a fast pace to chase that simply may not materialise here.

runners_data.name: Timely Salute
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on Good last time for Max Comley and Freddie Mitchell (3lb claimer), giving it a slight stamina edge in this trip; a natural hold-up type who needs others to force the pace, which Moment Of Light's solo lead makes difficult.

runners_data.name: Jerseygeordie
runners_data.note: All five career starts came on Standard Tapeta, making this turf debut a significant unknown; Harry Derham's yard is in form (2/3 T14) and Paul O'Brien takes the ride, but the horse's true style is hold-up and it arrives on completely unfamiliar ground conditions.

runners_data.name: Moment Of Light
runners_data.note: The race's sole pace-setter, with back-to-back wins at Stratford suggesting course-and-distance enthusiasm; 107 days off is worth noting but Skelton sends horses fit, and this horse is effectively the race-shaper — its jumping fluency at hurdles will be key.

runners_data.name: Nicolai
runners_data.note: Faded in the finish on its hurdles debut and carries a ⚠ fade flag; ran just 10 days ago (possible residual fatigue), and Neil Mulholland's yard is cold (0/9 T14) — a hold-up horse likely to find itself racing in a pack that never truly spreads out.

runners_data.name: Rajbello
runners_data.note: Six flat starts on Standard or Soft, none on Good turf, and Fergal O'Brien's yard is modest recently (2/10 T14); ran 9 days ago and the switch to jumping on unfamiliar ground adds risk for a horse whose hold-up style is already at a disadvantage in this shape.

runners_data.name: Zooter
runners_data.note: Consistent second-season form on Good ground (0W2P in similar conditions, placed in four of five career runs) and Sam Twiston-Davies is an experienced partner over hurdles; hold-up by inclination but has the scope to track closer if the pace is modest, making it one of the more pragmatic finishers in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Moment Of Light is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with Harry Skelton aboard for the powerful Dan Skelton yard, is expected to stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over 2m1f on Good ground at Newton Abbot. The remainder of the field — Hello Garda, Jerseygeordie, Nicolai, Rajbello, Zooter, and Timely Salute — are all natural hold-up or come-from-behind types, meaning Moment Of Light faces zero pressure and can control both the tempo and the race shape entirely on its own terms. This field holds considerably more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Rajbello, Nicolai, and Jerseygeordie are all redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice they will be racing behind Moment Of Light in a bunched, slowly-run pack, competing for the same ground late. A sedate, rail-hugging gallop set by an uncontested Moment Of Light on a track that suits front-runners heavily favours the prominent/front-running profile — horses that can track the pace closely and pounce early in the straight will have the clear edge, while pure hold-up horses arriving late face a stamina-sapping sprint-finish on ground that dries quickly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moment Of Light Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Moment Of Light is allowed to dictate a measured gallop with no horse willing or able to go with it.
scenarios.body: Skelton settles the favourite into an uncontested rhythm, pinging its hurdles, and the pace is precisely where the rider wants it throughout; the rest never close the gap until too late. Horses capable of tracking within three lengths of the leader are the primary beneficiaries, as pure hold-up types will face too large a deficit at the final flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse mapped to midfield manages to secure a tracking position and latches onto Moment Of Light early in the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse like Zooter or Hello Garda, enjoying the Good ground, slots into second or third early and is close enough to challenge when the tempo drops in the final half-mile. The lack of genuine pressure means the race resolves into a two-horse sprint from the last, favouring the horse with the best finishing constitution over the distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Benefit From Tactical Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Moment Of Light's lead becomes unsustainable and the pace collapses mid-race, compressing the field approaching the final hurdles.
scenarios.body: A stop-start, irregular gallop over an undulating Newton Abbot track scrambles the race and brings the entire trailing pack back into contention simultaneously at the last. Timely Salute and Hello Garda, both with Good-ground course form and patient jockey profiles, could pick up the pieces if the field concertinas in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems among the bunched hold-up horses disrupt the fancied runners late and a fresh horse sneaks through.
scenarios.body: With so many true hold-up types forced to race in close proximity in midfield, a clean run is not guaranteed and a horse that finds daylight first at the second-last could steal the spoils. Jerseygeordie, returning from a surface switch to turf and with Harry Derham's recent 2/3 trainer form, represents the most credible recipient of such a fortunate passage, though the probability remains low.

watchPoints.text: Moment Of Light's jumping at hurdles — if it makes an early error it surrenders the controlling position it holds over the entire race shape and the probability distribution shifts sharply toward closers.

The bunched hold-up group of Rajbello, Nicolai, and Jerseygeordie racing in close proximity to each other from the outset creates a genuine traffic-interference risk approaching the final two hurdles.
Timely Salute arrives on just one hurdles run (a win) — watch whether Freddie Mitchell elects to track Moment Of Light or drops in; the tactical decision made at the start will define its chance.

Nicolai ran only 10 days ago and carries a fade flag — watch its body language on the approach to the final hill at Newton Abbot, where tiring hurdlers typically drift and impede those finishing strongly behind them.

Jerseygeordie's reaction to turf for the first time is worth monitoring early — if it races keenly on an unfamiliar surface it could disrupt the rhythm of the hold-up group travelling immediately behind Moment Of Light.

races.name: Race Against Waste Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Crystal Mariner
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose best form at 16f on Good ground (placed at similar going 4 times) gives it strong stamina credentials here; Paddy Hanlon (5) rides and the 28-day gap is not a concern, though this is a step into a competitive maiden against fresher rivals.

runners_data.name: Happy Chandler
runners_data.note: Front-runner with headgear (h) who has won over 10f on Good ground and run well since, but a move to 17f is a clear stamina question; 47 days off and 10th on last Good-ground start over 16f both temper enthusiasm for a bold-from-front effort at this distance.

runners_data.name: Crackalackin
runners_data.note: Young prominent racer with four placed efforts at 16f on Good, making this trip its home track — Luke Scott (3) claims help with the weight, trainer Newland & Insole quiet (0/13 in 14 days) but form consistency makes this a solid place-profile runner regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: Explode
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden is a major booking and this four-year-old has two wins at 12f on Good, but its natural hold-up style will be slightly compromised in this shape with Crystal Mariner and Pay Attention also wanting late runs — effective but fractionally out of position, which tempers confidence in a clean run through.

runners_data.name: John Galt
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner alongside Happy Chandler, equipped with headgear (t) and a Good-ground hurdles win at 12f; Fergal O'Brien sits at 2/10 in 14 days which is a live yard angle, but the step to 17f and a directly contested lead is the key risk to his chance.

runners_data.name: Pay Attention
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor rides a horse that has run 12 times on similar going and placed once (1W5P), suggesting it handles Good reliably — headgear (t) worn, and the move from flat 8-10f trips to a hurdles test of 17f is a significant question mark, though the hold-up profile suits the expected race shape well.

races.paceDynamic: John Galt and Happy Chandler are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off, creating a genuinely competitive early pace over 2m1f on Good ground at Newton Abbot. Neither is likely to concede — John Galt has Fergal O'Brien's strong recent form behind him and a hurdles win at 12f, while Happy Chandler has front-run before and shapes as equally resolute. The resulting honest, contested gallop is likely to be maintained through the early stages, which on Good ground will stretch the field and place a premium on stamina and jumping efficiency rather than a late sprint. This race shape most favours hold-up or prominent types with the stamina to arrive late when the pace-setters have done the hard work — Crystal Mariner, Pay Attention, and Crackalackin are the profiles that stand to benefit most from two front-runners burning each other's petrol. The field holds more hold-up types than can naturally settle at the rear — Explode is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map because the shape is dominated at the back by Crystal Mariner and Pay Attention, meaning Explode is most likely to be pushed slightly wider and earlier than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stamina Verdict
scenarios.trigger: If John Galt and Happy Chandler lock horns early and sustain a genuine gallop, leaving both vulnerable in the final climb.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners take each other on through the body of the race, weakening their finishing reserves on Good ground, and the race opens up for those tracking from just off the pace in the final quarter-mile; Crackalackin's consistent form at this trip and Crystal Mariner's hold-up profile give them the best angle to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Chandler surrenders the lead early and John Galt gets an uncontested, controlled tempo that preserves his stamina reserves.
scenarios.body: John Galt settles into a rhythm without pressure, controls the pace to suit himself, and has enough to repel challengers jumping the final hurdle; his Fergal O'Brien trainer form (2/10 in 14 days) and prior hurdles win on Good ground underpin this outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If Crackalackin or Pay Attention tracks the leaders efficiently and the pace slackens in the middle stages, allowing a prominent type to surge clear.
scenarios.body: A slightly reduced gallop in the middle portion of the race means the held-up horses never quite get the searching test they need, and Crackalackin's string of placed efforts at this distance demonstrates it handles a softer test well; Pay Attention's Good-ground profile (1W5P at sim going) supports the same outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Swooper Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a genuinely fierce pace and the race breaks open wide enough for a hold-up horse to produce a devastating late run.
scenarios.body: Crystal Mariner's hold-up style and prior form at 16f would suit this scenario perfectly, and Pay Attention's Good-ground record suggests it can stay on; however, with Explode operating slightly out of its ideal hold-up position due to field congestion, the window for a clean late run is narrow.

watchPoints.text: John Galt and Happy Chandler — watch whether either blinks at the start of the back straight; if one capitulates early, the tempo collapses and the race shape flips entirely from contested to controlled.

Explode — Harry Cobden may be forced to ride closer than ideal given the congestion of hold-up types in this small field; watch its position at the third hurdle as a sign of whether it gets a clean run.

Pay Attention — stepping sharply up in distance from flat-paced 8-10f form to a 17f hurdles test; if it struggles to settle or is outpaced jumping, its Good-ground stamina base is genuinely untested at this level.

Crackalackin — the most consistent placer in the field at this trip and going; watch it track the leaders from the second circuit because if it jumps cleanly throughout it could be the most straightforward beneficiary of a contested early pace.

races.name: St. Austell Brewery Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Melton Mossy
runners_data.note: Lightly campaigned, 108 days since last run is the key query, though trainer Mrs C Williams has four wins from five on similar going; a natural hold-up horse whose best form comes over 19-20f on Good — dropping to 2m½f may be a shade short, but prior wins at 16f show adaptability.

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: In flying form with three consecutive wins before a spin at Huntingdon, and Luke Scott's 3lb claim is a live asset on just 163lbs; a true hold-up type who has won on Good at 17-18f, so the trip and going are both squarely in his favour — 10 days since last run poses no concern given recent frequency.

runners_data.name: Juggernaut
runners_data.note: The sole pace-setter whose style fit at 0.92 flags that front-running is not his absolute comfort zone — he has placed eight times from 15 without winning, and Chad Bament (5lb claimer) gives him a weight advantage; Good ground is fine and a trip of 18f suits better than today's longer 2m½f, which is a legitimate query.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: Trainer Bridgwater has a quiet 14-day record (0/4), and the visor is a notable headgear flag for a horse who has been placed at OR=87 on Good; genuinely a hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map due to field composition, so do not read his mapped position as tactical aggression — he will settle and close as usual.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies takes the ride for the family yard and brings considerable experience to a mare with five consecutive placed runs — she has never actually won but her consistency is striking; another true closer whose position on the pace map reflects field congestion at the rear rather than any change in running style, and 23 days since last run is a routine gap.

races.paceDynamic: Juggernaut is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to press him, Chad Bament can dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable gallop over 2m½f on Good ground at Newton Abbot. The three hold-up types — Melton Mossy, Saint Polo, and Most Wanted — will have to settle in behind, while Miss Denver and Most Wanted are redistributed to midfield on the pace map because the field holds more true hold-up horses than can all occupy the rear; in reality, Most Wanted and Miss Denver are natural closers and are unlikely to be racing any closer than their instincts dictate. With Juggernaut controlling a single-figure field at an uncontested tempo, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a strong finishing kick who can close over the final two fences — a shape that rewards horses who travel well through the race and peak late rather than those needing to make headway against a pressured pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Juggernaut Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Juggernaut sets a steady, uncontested pace and the hold-up horses find enough cover to produce a late challenge at the last.
scenarios.body: Juggernaut's easy lead slows the race into a tactical exercise, compressing the field and giving the genuine closers — Melton Mossy and Saint Polo — a perfect jumping, travelling race before they unleash late; both have strong form on Good ground over trips up to 20f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Juggernaut Idles, Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Juggernaut bowls along at a comfortable gallop, jumps fluently, and the hold-up horses simply cannot reel him in over the final two fences.
scenarios.body: A small, polite field with no genuine pace pressure can gift a front-runner a winning lead that never gets pegged back, especially if the closers are shuffled wide or lose momentum at a fence; Juggernaut's consistency (eight placed runs from 15 on similar ground) speaks to his staying power even if wins have eluded him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Scrappy Winner
scenarios.trigger: If mistakes or jumping errors disrupt Juggernaut's lead and force a chaotic reshuffle approaching the home turn.
scenarios.body: A small-field chase over 2m½f can turn on a single jumping blunder, and if Juggernaut fiddles a fence and loses his rhythm, the midfield-mapped Most Wanted or Miss Denver — both recording consistent placed runs — could emerge in a scrambled finish; both are, however, racing slightly out of their natural hold-up role in terms of expected trajectory.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Outstayed
scenarios.trigger: If the pace dries up too much and the closers leave their runs too late, leaving them with too much to do from the final fence.
scenarios.body: In a five-runner field with a genuine front-runner in control, over-reliance on a finishing burst can leave hold-up types caught flat-footed if the tempo was never truly strong enough to create a lead worth closing; Melton Mossy's 108-day layoff adds a small fitness question that could blunt his closing speed in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Juggernaut's front-running at a style-fit of 0.92 combined with Chad Bament's 5lb claim means any jumping error in the lead could be catastrophic — watch his jumping at the open ditch closely.
Melton Mossy's 108-day absence is the largest fitness unknown in the race; if Adam Wedge has to push earlier than usual to get competitive, his hold-up profile could be completely negated.

Saint Polo's rapid back-to-back campaign (three wins, now 10 days since last run) could either signal peak fitness or a horse that has been asked plenty — watch his jumping fluency as a proxy for freshness.

With three genuine hold-up types (Melton Mossy, Saint Polo, Most Wanted, Miss Denver) all wanting to come from behind Juggernaut, watch how quickly they establish their order in the early stages — a slow-jumping start by any one of them will leave them with significantly more to do than intended.

Miss Denver's string of five placed runs without a win raises the question of whether she finds enough when it matters — watch her response after the last fence specifically, as that is where her record suggests she may weaken or idle.

races.name: Devonport Royal Dockyard Social Club Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Jager Time
runners_data.note: Consistent, genuine staying form on Good — wins at 25-26f, solid sim-going record of 11/14, and Fergal O'Brien's yard is hitting a 2/10 strike in the 14-day window; 50 days off, but proven fresh and a natural hold-up type who will need to be ridden handily to be effective in this pace-light shape.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Skipper
runners_data.note: Recent run just 7d ago could leave him short of full freshness, though Mickey Bowen's yard is firing at 6/23 and Shane Fenelon (5) provides a valuable 5lb claim; naturally held up at the rear, he will need to be more positionally active than ideal if this race is run at a steady tempo.

runners_data.name: Masterdream
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie wearing, nine-year-old with a strong recent string of 133-P3 and a 13/15 sim-going strike — his form is genuine on this surface at this sort of trip; his natural inclination is to race from behind, and in a small field where hold-up slots are crowded, he may find traffic or position less ideal than his ability deserves, tempering his chance.

runners_data.name: My Girl Katie
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — five wins from her last six starts including three successive victories over 26f on Good, and she lands at the peak of her form; Grace Harris's yard is active at 3/21 in 14 days, but My Girl Katie's STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder that in faster-run races, front-runners can be vulnerable to a more prominent chaser who travels kindly behind her.

runners_data.name: Bashful Boy
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old carrying tongue-tie and blinkers, and his handicap mark of 89 reflects a gradual decline — best efforts recently were placed third and fourth over shorter; a true hold-up type forced into midfield positioning, 47 days off adds a fitness question and his recent form suggests he is operating below the required level.

runners_data.name: Henry Box Brown
runners_data.note: Won over 23f on Good last time, and his 11/15 sim-going record confirms he handles this surface well; Adam Wedge is a capable claimer and the horse showed enough last time to be live at these weights, though as another genuine rear-runner in a field already full of them, securing a clean run from a workable position will be a real challenge.

runners_data.name: Alberts Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent placed record — three thirds and two others in recent starts, all on or near Good ground — but his OR of 83 reflects the ceiling of his ability; James Best takes the ride for a yard with just 0/1 in 14 days, and as a true hold-up type shown in midfield by necessity, the redistribution means he is unlikely to get the detached run that suits him best.

races.paceDynamic: My Girl Katie is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, she will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 3m2½f trip at Newton Abbot. The pace will be honest but not searching — a lone leader dictating from the front on Good ground creates a rhythm that suits those who can travel close to the pace rather than those needing a late injection of pace from far back. Jager Time and Fairlawn Skipper are the most naturally suited closers, though both have shown versatility in good going at staying trips. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Masterdream, Bashful Boy, Henry Box Brown, and Alberts Bay are all true rear-runners pushed into midfield on the map, with Masterdream and Henry Box Brown — both recent placed runners at this sort of trip on Good — most likely to actually secure a workable midfield position. This shape strongly favours prominent or close-tracking profiles who can travel within striking range of My Girl Katie and pounce from the home turn, rather than genuine hold-up horses forced to make up ground from further back than natural.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Chase
scenarios.trigger: If My Girl Katie leads unchallenged and sets a fair pace that rewards close-tracking profiles.
scenarios.body: My Girl Katie dictates from the front on her own terms, and the horses closest to her travelling sweetly will have first run from the home turn; over 3m2½f on Good ground, this is a stamina-and-position race, not a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If My Girl Katie goes too fast early and fades, opening the race up for those with reserves.
scenarios.body: A strong early gallop from the leader sets up a punishing final circuit, leaving the door open for a hold-up horse who has tracked at a distance and stayed fresh; Henry Box Brown or Jager Time, both proven at the trip on Good, are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Delivery, Prominent Types Outpaced
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that repositioned hold-up horses land in their natural rhythm by mistake.
scenarios.body: Masterdream or Henry Box Brown, both honest performers on Good ground at staying trips, find themselves in a better tactical spot than the map suggests and finish with purpose; Masterdream's consistency at 3m-plus with a tongue-tie gives him a credible claims if this scenario materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that the field bunches and the race becomes a scramble from two out.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run race over 3m2½f compresses the field and reduces the advantage of those with positional sense, giving lower-rated finishers like Alberts Bay or Bashful Boy a flattering opportunity; Alberts Boy's consistent placed form at the trip on Good is the modest case for his involvement.

watchPoints.text: My Girl Katie's early pace will be the defining factor — watch whether she bowls along or is permitted a soft early gallop, as the former could compromise her stamina, the latter could allow closer-tracking rivals to pounce before she quickens.

Henry Box Brown, Masterdream, and Alberts Bay are all genuine hold-up horses competing for the same rear positions — watch for traffic problems or checks at hurdles as they negotiate their way through a bunched rear group.

Fairlawn Skipper ran just 7 days ago — watch his body language in the parade ring and early in the race; if he travels labouredly, the quick turnaround may have blunted his chance despite the yard's form.

Jager Time is 50 days off but has proven course-fresh before — watch his jumping early; Fergal O'Brien's runners often need a fence or two to find their rhythm on a return and a clean round is essential over a trip this long.

Bashful Boy's tongue-tie and blinkers combination is worth monitoring — headgear changes in staying hurdles can occasionally sharpen a horse's early effort, which would be out of character and could disrupt the race shape if he jumps off keenly.

races.name: Par Inn Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: Clearly the dominant pace angle here — Dan Skelton's four-year-old arrives in fine form (111 in last three completed runs) with strong similar-going credentials (10/12, 4W6P), and 50 days off is not a concern for a yard operating at 8/24 in the 14-day window; the STYLE_FIT tag is academic given it will lead naturally in this field with zero front-running competition.

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up type for John Joseph Hanlon, returning quickly on just seven days' rest with a tongue-tie fitted, but recent form figures of 4U439F are alarming and the yard has fired only 1/12 runners in the last fortnight — the similar-going record (14/15, 1W5P) hints at place potential rather than winning punch at this point.

runners_data.name: Arctic Voyage
runners_data.note: Michael Blake's four-year-old is the most eye-catching hold-up performer in the field on raw form (P1-121 in recent starts, 3W from 5), though a 66-day absence and a yard running at 0/3 in 14 days tempers confidence; if it has trained on, it is the hold-up horse most likely to threaten Edelak in any scenario where the pace even slightly slackens.

runners_data.name: Ellerton
runners_data.note: Joe Tizzard's six-year-old is in truth a deep hold-up type — tongue-tied, 11 days fresh off a win, and the yard is red-hot at 1/1 in 14 days — but it is mapped to midfield purely because this field is saturated with rear-of-field runners and it cannot be further back than it already is; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that racing closer than natural may not suit, and the OR drop to 106 from heavier weights in longer trips is worth noting.

races.paceDynamic: Edelak is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this four-runner field and will lead from the front unchallenged, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m1f on Good ground at Newton Abbot. With War Correspondent, Arctic Voyage, and Ellerton all genuine hold-up types, Edelak faces zero pressure for the lead and can dictate every stride, controlling tempo and conserving energy through the early stages. At this distance on Good turf with a lone front-runner and three hold-up horses tracking at varying distances, the race will likely develop into a measured contest until the final two hurdles, where Edelak's ability to quicken from the front becomes the key weapon. This shape strongly favours a front-runner who can control fractions and pick up when asked — hold-up horses will need Edelak to either slow dramatically or blunder at a flight to get into the race; Ellerton, though mapped to midfield due to field redistribution, is a true hold-up type and is unlikely to be any closer to the pace than War Correspondent or Arctic Voyage in reality.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak dictates an uncontested, steady pace and picks up smoothly in the straight.
scenarios.body: Edelak leads wire-to-wire with no rivals willing or able to challenge early, effectively setting its own race — Harry Skelton can switch Edelak off behind the pace fractions it sets itself, conserving enough to repel chasers late. The hold-up horses are left to make up ground on a horse that has never been under pressure, and on Good ground over 2m1f, Edelak's form figures of 111 in similar conditions make it the clear profile beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak's early fractions are slow enough that hold-up horses travel powerfully into the race and produce a decisive late challenge.
scenarios.body: A very steady pace paradoxically can suit closers who time their run to perfection from two out, with the race only igniting up the straight — Arctic Voyage's excellent recent form (P1-121) and proven ability over similar Good-ground trips makes it the most dangerous hold-up type to produce such a challenge. War Correspondent's poor recent string (4U439F) makes it a less likely beneficiary even in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse After Error
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak makes a significant jumping error mid-race, disrupting its rhythm and allowing hold-up horses to surge past.
scenarios.body: A front-runner unseated, refused, or badly hampered at a hurdle opens the race dramatically, with Arctic Voyage and Ellerton — both proven winners — best placed to capitalise if travelling well at the time. Ellerton's tongue-tie and Joe Tizzard's recent yard form (1/1 in 14 days) adds minor interest, but this scenario depends on external misfortune rather than planned tactics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Develops Into Slog
scenarios.trigger: If the Good ground rides slower than reported and a grinding gallop suits the most durable stayer in the field.
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly taxing surface would level the playing field between Edelak's front-running economy and the stamina reserves of hold-up types, potentially rewarding the horse with the deepest reserves — Arctic Voyage's 3W from 5 recent runs and proven class at this trip makes it the profile fit. War Correspondent's poor current form means it is an unlikely beneficiary even in an endurance-based shape.

watchPoints.text: Edelak's jumping is the single biggest variable — if Harry Skelton gets it jumping slickly throughout, this race looks tailor-made for a wire-to-wire success given the complete absence of pace pressure.

Arctic Voyage's 66-day absence for a yard (Michael Blake, 0/3 in 14 days) that shows no recent signs of form means it must be taken on trust — watch the market for signs it has been freshened purposefully rather than returning under-prepared.

War Correspondent is sharply turned out on just seven days' rest, but the 4U439F recent form string includes an unseated and a fall — jumping safety at pace under Paddy Hanlon (5lb claimer) should be monitored early, as any interference could affect the small field significantly.

Ellerton's tongue-tie is applied in the context of a horse whose Tizzard yard is operating at maximum recent strike-rate (1/1 in 14 days) — if it travels unexpectedly prominently rather than settling at the rear, that would be a noteworthy in-running signal worth tracking from the first flight.

races.name: Grandad Swales Happy 80th Birthday Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up type whose best form — a second over 2m4f on good — fits both the trip and conditions; has run 9 times including recent Goodwood form (7d ago) so freshness is not a concern, and the tongue strap is retained, but a poor run record of 0 wins from 15 similar-going starts does temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Jetty May
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls has had only 0 winners from 2 runners in the past 14 days but Jetty May carries a win on good ground over 22f and the return from 76 days off is the key question; a hold-up style perfectly suited to the contested pace scenario and the tongue tie plus cheekpieces suggest connections are motivated to get a result today.

runners_data.name: Hatos
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will try to make every yard alongside Mcgregors Charge; the 76-day absence and two pulled-up runs in last two outings are genuine flags, but the Tizzard yard has fired in 1 from 1 in the 14-day window, and if he gets first run at the last he could pinch it if the duel is less fierce than expected.

runners_data.name: Mr McWhinny
runners_data.note: Strong recent form including a win 19 days ago at a shorter trip (17f) is the headline here; at heart a hold-up/rear-of-field horse, he is pushed into midfield on this map because the pack of true front-runners leaves no room at the back, and racing further forward than he prefers marginally compromises his chance in a strongly-run race.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: Has a win on good ground over 24f and consistent place form in this kind of handicap, making him a credible front-running threat; a 5lb claimer (Jack Stenhouse) reduces the weight and the Polly Gundry yard has been ticking along quietly, but 0 wins from 15 similar-going starts suggests he is better placed as a pace-maker than a race-winner.

races.paceDynamic: Hatos and Mcgregors Charge are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over 2m5f at Newton Abbot, creating a genuinely contested gallop on good ground that is unlikely to relent. With two horses fighting for supremacy across the early fences, the pace should be honest rather than dawdling, stretching the field and putting a premium on jumping fluency and stamina. This race shape favours hold-up horses who can track the battle from a safe distance and arrive with a late run — My Cullen and Jetty May are the natural profile beneficiaries. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place cleanly at the rear; Mr McWhinny is a genuine hold-up horse shown in midfield, but Hatos and Mcgregors Charge are far more likely to actually secure the front positions given their natural style, with Mr McWhinny likely to find himself racing slightly further forward than ideal given the contested nature ahead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Hatos and Mcgregors Charge trade blows throughout, burning each other off and leaving the door open for a fresh hold-up horse to pounce.
scenarios.body: The sustained duel saps both front-runners before the final fences, leaving them vulnerable to a horse who has conserved energy tracking from off the pace. My Cullen and Jetty May are ideally profiled for exactly this scenario, with both showing good form on good ground at distances around this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacer Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Mcgregors Charge or Hatos breaks clear early and the other capitulates, allowing one horse to control an unchallenged gallop.
scenarios.body: A solo front-runner on good ground over 2m5f at Newton Abbot can dictate terms, conserving enough energy to hold on if the pace is measured. Hatos has the higher OR and better recent course form, making this the slightly more plausible version of the scenario if Mcgregors Charge blunders or drops away.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong end-to-end and a hold-up horse produces an eye-catching late surge from last to first.
scenarios.body: Mr McWhinny is the horse most likely to fill this role if he finds his natural position despite being mapped to midfield, though his style fit is discounted here given the redistribution caveat. Jetty May, with a win on similar going and the Paul Nicholls yard in decent conditional form, represents the cleaner profile in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage, Survivor Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the contested gallop produces jumping errors, fallers or a messy race that turns into a test of attrition with few standing at the finish.
scenarios.body: Newton Abbot's fences can catch out tired horses in handicap chases and a strong early pace raises the risk of mistakes at key fences late on. Mcgregors Charge, the lower-rated front-runner, or My Cullen as a hold-up survivor could benefit if others exit the race.

watchPoints.text: Hatos and Mcgregors Charge — if both attack the lead hard from flag fall, watch whether either capitulates before halfway, as a one-sided duel would fundamentally reshape the tactical picture.
Mr McWhinny — a genuine hold-up horse forced to race further forward than ideal; if he cannot slot in behind the leaders as planned, his finishing effort in the straight may be blunted.

Jetty May — 76 days off the track for a six-year-old who has been well backed in headgear before; if she is short of match sharpness she will not have enough petrol in the tank to deliver a late run over this stamina-testing 2m5f.

My Cullen — raced just 7 days ago and drops back slightly in trip, so watch her jumping in the early stages; a horse who has been in action recently sometimes takes a fence cheaply and an error at a key fence at Newton Abbot could cost her any chance in a small field.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: A front-runner carrying top-weight for John Joseph Hanlon, she has the race to herself on pace terms and that is her clearest asset; her recent form shows no win in 15 similar-going starts and the STYLE_FIT flag suggests she is technically racing slightly out of her ideal pattern, so her advantage is positional rather than form-based.

runners_data.name: Devon Red
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's lightly-raced seven-year-old has placed over 2m on Good and handles this going (2/2), but the unknown quantity of the step to 2m5½f is the key question — if the stamina holds, J M Quinlan can place him prominently from an unclassified style base.

runners_data.name: Ocean Heights
runners_data.note: David Pipe's veteran travels prominently and boasts solid place form at this trip and beyond on Good ground; Jack Tudor is a shrewd pilot and nine hurdles suits a horse who places regularly but whose lone win here came on similar ground — a clean round at the front could be rewarded.

runners_data.name: Mystic Wind
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this lightly-raced four-year-old who holds a natural hold-up style and headgear (ht), but has failed to place in any of her four career runs on Good; the 50-day absence and lack of winning form on this going make her a significant each-way outsider regardless of scenario.

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's six-year-old is the most credible closer in the field with two wins from ten Good-ground starts and a genuine hold-up style that is not compromised by redistribution; Callum Pritchard rode him to victory ten days ago and the horse arrives in form, giving this profile its best chance of landing a late blow.

runners_data.name: Gilded Glance
runners_data.note: Jane Williams's six-year-old is a true hold-up specialist whose last four runs show no placing at all, and after 146 days off she returns here with the further handicap of being pushed forward from her natural rear position — a punishing combination that makes a winning effort very hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Captain Connor
runners_data.note: A natural closer for Clare Ellam whose race record contains a placed run over 2m2f on Good but mostly defeats in both Good and Soft; having been shifted into midfield on the map because rear positions are over-subscribed, Brendan Powell will need to find gaps the shape of this race is unlikely to create.

runners_data.name: Ghost Jury
runners_data.note: Kayley Woollacott's seven-year-old has shown consistent hold-up form — placed three times in 13 similar-going starts — and Ghost Jury ran second at this course over 2m2f which is encouraging; Ben Jones will nonetheless struggle to get his horse's true position at the rear in a field this loaded with genuine closers, which blunts the late-run threat.

races.paceDynamic: Mother Ship is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, facing no meaningful pace pressure from this field, should be able to dictate a controlled, even gallop from the front over 2m5½f on Good ground. Ocean Heights will track prominently and apply some company from second or third, but with no horse capable of genuinely attacking Mother Ship's lead, the tempo is expected to be sustainable rather than searching. The three genuine hold-up horses — Gilded Glance, Captain Connor, and Ghost Jury — have been displaced into midfield on the map because there are more true closers in this field than the rear can accommodate; in practice, one or more may end up further back than is ideal, compromising their ability to land a telling blow. This race shape — a lone, uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace on Good ground over a staying trip — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and produce a clean jump-and-stay performance in the final mile, giving the edge to prominent racers and any hold-up horse with the stamina and class to close from an honest but not punishing pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mother Ship Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mother Ship is allowed to stride into a clear lead early and dictates an uncontested, galloping tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Mother Ship sets a comfortable rhythm, jumps accurately, and the field never coalesces to challenge until too late; her prominent rivals cannot raise enough pace to reel her in late. Horses who travelled prominently and conserved energy closest to her — Ocean Heights chief among them — are best placed to mount any late challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean Heights or Devon Red tracks the pace efficiently and outstays Mother Ship in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A steady early pace means the horses who press from second and third have their stamina reserves intact when the race becomes serious from three out; Ocean Heights has the form to place and Devon Red's lightly-raced profile suits a staying test on Good ground. The front-runner tires late and a close-tracking rival picks up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses after the final flight and a horse from the back of the midfield finishes powerfully through tired rivals.
scenarios.body: Makinbecon is the best-credentialled closer with two wins on Good over this sort of trip and is not tagged out of role in the same way as Gilded Glance, Captain Connor, or Ghost Jury; if the gallop was genuinely honest enough to string the field out, a strong finisher can arrive late. The redistributed hold-up types — Gilded Glance, Captain Connor, Ghost Jury — are less likely to benefit given they cannot secure their natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field runs in a tight cluster throughout and the race is only truly decided at the last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Without genuine pace pressure, the field could concertina behind Mother Ship, creating a sprint finish that rewards class and jumping accuracy at the death over pure stamina. Mystic Wind, handled by Harry Skelton, could capitalise if the race becomes a dash from home, though her hold-up profile and lack of wins on Good ground remain concerns.

watchPoints.text: Mother Ship's jumping — if she pings the hurdles and settles in front, she is very hard to peg back in this pace-less race; watch for any early errors that let Ocean Heights close the gap.

Gilded Glance (146-day absence) and Mystic Wind (50 days off) both return from significant breaks — monitor their paddock behaviour and early race positioning as fitness unknowns could unravel the map entirely.

Makinbecon ran only 10 days ago and won; a quick turnaround can blunt a hold-up horse's finishing kick on Good ground, so watch whether Callum Pritchard is travelling with his usual fluency approaching the final mile.

Ghost Jury has course form at Newton Abbot (2nd, 2m2f) and is the only true hold-up type with identifiable local track knowledge — worth noting if the race develops into a stamina grind rather than a controlled procession.

Devon Red's trip stamina is entirely unproven beyond 2m1f — watch how J M Quinlan rides him in the first half of the race; if ridden prominently and the horse flattens out after the third-last, the stamina ceiling has been found.
